      Why FortiPass

      Real cryptographic randomness

      Every character comes from crypto.getRandomValues() with rejection sampling, so there is no modulo bias and no predictable seed — unlike generators built on Math.random().

      Honest strength numbers

      Instead of a vague “strong” badge you get the actual entropy in bits and an estimated cracking time for an offline attacker making 100 billion guesses per second.

      Nothing leaves your device

      No accounts, no analytics, no network requests. Your settings are saved locally so the generator is ready the way you like it next time; the passwords themselves are never stored.

      Install it and go offline

      FortiPass is a progressive web app. Add it to your home screen or desktop and it keeps working on a plane, in a server room or with the network unplugged.

      Choosing a good password

      • Length beats complexity. A 16-character password from this generator needs about 2.5 trillion years to brute-force; an 8-character one, about 3 hours. See the full crack-time table.
      • Never reuse a password. One breach elsewhere should not unlock your email. Unique passwords are what a manager is for.
      • Use a passphrase for what you must type. Device logins and your password-manager vault are easier as six or more random words.
      • Turn on two-factor authentication — or use a passkey. Even a perfect password is no help once it has been phished. Passkeys and hardware security keys resist phishing; codes from an app or a text message can be phished along with the password.
      • Change a password when there is a reason. A breach or a shared secret — not an arbitrary 90-day calendar rule.

      Questions people ask

      Are the generated passwords sent anywhere?

      No. Everything is generated in your browser tab with the Web Crypto API, and the page's Content Security Policy forbids its scripts to make any network request. Your browser's network panel shows FortiPass loading its own files and nothing else — nothing you generate ever goes out. Only your settings are remembered on your device; generated values never are.

      How long should my password be?

      For anything stored in a password manager, use 16 characters or more with all character types — that is over 100 bits of entropy and out of reach of brute force. For a password you have to type from memory, a passphrase of six or more words (about 77.5 bits) is a better trade between security and your patience.

      What does “entropy” actually mean?

      Entropy is a measure of unpredictability expressed in bits. Each additional bit doubles the number of guesses needed. FortiPass calls anything below 50 bits weak, 50 to 70 bits fair, 70 bits or more strong, and 90 bits or more excellent for essentially any threat model.

      Is a passphrase of real words safe?

      Yes, provided the words are picked at random by a computer rather than by you. FortiPass selects from the 7,776-word EFF list using a cryptographic random number generator, so every word adds 12.9 bits: six words is roughly 77.5 bits. The figure shown under your passphrase is calculated from the real list size, not guessed.

      Can I use FortiPass offline or install it?

      Yes. After the first visit the app is cached on your device, so it loads without a connection. Most browsers will also offer to install it — look for “Install app” or “Add to Home Screen”.

      Does the strength checker upload what I type?

      No. The check runs on heuristics and entropy maths that ship with the page — dictionary words, a list of very common passwords, leet swaps, repeated blocks, keyboard sequences, years and character variety. Nothing is sent over the network, and the field is wiped when you leave the page.

      Is FortiPass open source?

      Yes, under the MIT licence. The source code is on GitHub, including the tests that check the randomness is uniform and the entropy maths exact.
